title: Could One Phone Call Lead to the 28th Amendment?

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的球队。

I use a different starting word every day.

And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，庆祝175年来致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受特别优惠，网址是nytimes.com/subscribe。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The pitch to President Biden from dozens of congressional Democrats is simple.
sentences.zh: 数十位民主党国会议员向拜登总统提出的诉求很简单。

sentences.en: With a single phone call, they've told him.
sentences.zh: 他们通过一通电话告诉了他。

sentences.en: He can revolutionize women's rights and revive his damaged legacy in the process.
sentences.zh: 他可以借此彻底改变女性权利，并重振他受损的政治遗产。

sentences.en: The question now is whether they're right.
sentences.zh: 现在的问题是他们是否正确。

sentences.en: And even if they are, whether Biden is willing to do it.
sentences.zh: 即使他们是对的，拜登是否愿意这样做。

sentences.en: It's Monday, December 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月23日，星期一。

sentences.en: Hello, Annie Carney.
sentences.zh: 你好，安妮·卡尼。

sentences.en: Hello, Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 你好，迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: You are actually joining us from inside Congress, where there has been lots of news over the past few days.
sentences.zh: 你现在是在国会大厦内连线我们，过去几天那里发生了很多新闻。

sentences.en: And we are grateful for you making time for us.
sentences.zh: 我们很感谢你抽出时间接受采访。

sentences.en: I'm happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能在这里。

sentences.en: I'm sitting on the house side in a small recording booth.
sentences.zh: 我正坐在众议院那边的一个小型录音间里。

sentences.en: Yeah, it looks very cozy.
sentences.zh: 是的，看起来很舒适。

sentences.en: This story begins with a quest to do something that, from today's perspective, a lot of people might think is already baked into American law, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 这个故事始于一项追求，从今天的角度来看，很多人可能认为这已经是美国法律中理所当然的一部分，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: So tell us the whole story of why it's actually not.
sentences.zh: 那么请告诉我们为什么事实并非如此的完整故事。

sentences.en: So this is a story that starts about a century ago, and it's a pretty remarkable story about a very simple idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个始于大约一个世纪前，关于一个非常简单理念的非凡故事。

sentences.en: And that is that men and women should be equal under the law in the United States, and that discrimination based on sex should be prohibited.
sentences.zh: 那就是在美国，男女在法律面前应该平等，基于性别的歧视应该被禁止。

sentences.en: That's the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这么简单。

sentences.en: But it's never actually been put into the Constitution in such plain language.
sentences.zh: 但它从未以如此直白的语言被写入宪法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That men and women must be treated equal under the eyes of law.
sentences.zh: 即男女在法律面前必须受到平等待遇。

sentences.en: That's actually not language in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 这实际上并不是美国宪法中的措辞。

sentences.en: Constitution.
sentences.zh: 宪法。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: You have the 14th Amendment, which has an equal protection clause.
sentences.zh: 你有第14修正案，其中包含平等保护条款。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mention sex specifically.
sentences.zh: 但它没有明确提到性别。

sentences.en: And this passed in the 1860s, decades before women were even guaranteed the right to vote.
sentences.zh: 而且它是在19世纪60年代通过的，比女性获得投票权保障还要早几十年。

sentences.en: This existed when married women in many states couldn't even own property under their own names.
sentences.zh: 在那个年代，许多州的已婚女性甚至不能以自己的名义拥有财产。

sentences.en: So this was not really about sex equality.
sentences.zh: 所以这并不是真正关于性别平等。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It will eventually apply to sex equality cases, the 14th Amendment, but it doesn't, as you say, specifically mention sex.
sentences.zh: 第14修正案最终会适用于性别平等案件，但正如你所说，它没有明确提到性别。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: So in 1923, a suffragist named Alice Paul comes up with the idea that the United States needs a constitutional amendment specifically addressing women's equality.
sentences.zh: 所以在1923年，一位名叫爱丽丝·保罗的女性参政权论者提出了一个想法，即美国需要一项专门针对女性平等的宪法修正案。

sentences.en: And she actually gets something in front of lawmakers, but it doesn't really go anywhere or get any traction for years.
sentences.zh: 她确实把提案提交到了立法者面前，但多年来并没有取得任何进展或反响。

sentences.en: For 72 years in their struggle to get the right to vote.
sentences.zh: 在她们争取投票权的72年斗争中。

sentences.en: Until the late 1960s, when the women's rights movement is really blossoming.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪60年代末，女性权利运动真正蓬勃发展之时。

sentences.en: Welcome to the new wave of feminism.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到新一波女权主义浪潮。

sentences.en: Welcome to each other.
sentences.zh: 欢迎彼此。

sentences.en: Welcome home.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回家。

sentences.en: And suddenly there is excitement around this idea.
sentences.zh: 突然间，人们对这个想法感到兴奋。

sentences.en: And what happens once the women's rights movement is in blossom?
sentences.zh: 那么当女性权利运动蓬勃发展时发生了什么？

sentences.en: I would like to discuss with you briefly the Equal Rights Amendment.
sentences.zh: 我想和你简要讨论一下《平等权利修正案》。

sentences.en: So in 1971, a Democratic lawmaker in the House introduces a bill called the Equal Rights Amendment.
sentences.zh: 所以在1971年，众议院的一位民主党议员提出了一项名为《平等权利修正案》的法案。

sentences.en: The Equal Rights Amendment gives women rights that they do not now have.
sentences.zh: 《平等权利修正案》赋予了女性她们目前所不具备的权利。

sentences.en: And it passes with overwhelming margins from both parties.
sentences.zh: 它以两党压倒性的票数通过了。

sentences.en: And then a year later, it passes the Senate where the final vote was 84 to 8 in favor of the Equal Rights Amendment.
sentences.zh: 一年后，它在参议院以84票对8票的最终结果通过，支持《平等权利修正案》。

sentences.en: Tonight, after a 49-year struggle, a constitutional amendment appears on the way proclaiming once and for all that women have all the same rights as that other sex.
sentences.zh: 今晚，经过49年的斗争，一项宪法修正案似乎即将出台，一劳永逸地宣告女性拥有与另一性别完全相同的权利。

sentences.en: But there's one more step that needs to happen for an amendment to become part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 但要使一项修正案成为宪法的一部分，还需要再迈出一步。

sentences.en: And that is it needs three-quarters of the states to adopt it.
sentences.zh: 那就是需要四分之三的州通过它。

sentences.en: For today, Indiana became the 35th, leaving the Women's Rights Declaration just three states away from becoming the 27th Amendment to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 今天，印第安纳州成为了第35个通过的州，这意味着《女性权利宣言》距离成为宪法第27修正案仅差三个州。

sentences.en: And 35 states pass it in just five years, leaving it just three states short of ratification.
sentences.zh: 在短短五年内，35个州通过了它，距离批准仅差三个州。

sentences.en: So it looks like it's just sailing smoothly through the process of becoming a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来它正在顺利地通过成为宪法修正案的程序。

sentences.en: I get fed up with the women's liberationists running down motherhood and saying that it's a...
sentences.zh: 我受够了那些贬低母性并说它是一种……的女性解放主义者。

sentences.en: Until it runs up against vocal opposition led by a conservative woman named Phyllis Schlafly.
sentences.zh: 直到它遇到了以保守派女性菲利斯·施拉夫利为首的强烈反对。

sentences.en: The Equal Rights Amendment will take away from women some of the most important rights that they now possess.
sentences.zh: 《平等权利修正案》将剥夺女性目前拥有的一些最重要的权利。

sentences.en: She's a self-described housewife, an anti-feminist Republican who wages war against the ERA.
sentences.zh: 她是一位自称家庭主妇的反女权主义共和党人，对《平等权利修正案》发动了战争。

sentences.en: First of all, it will have a powerful, dramatic, adverse effect on the rights of the draft-age girl.
sentences.zh: 首先，它将对适龄征兵女孩的权利产生强大、剧烈且不利的影响。

sentences.en: Her basic argument is that it would actually take away rights from women.
sentences.zh: 她的基本论点是，它实际上会剥夺女性的权利。

sentences.en: That every 18-year-old girl will be compelled to be given a draft number and to be available for call-up.
sentences.zh: 即每个18岁的女孩都将被迫获得征兵编号，并随时准备应征入伍。

sentences.en: By eroding traditional gender roles.
sentences.zh: 通过侵蚀传统的性别角色。

sentences.en: The second category of women who will be hurt by the Equal Rights Amendment are wives.
sentences.zh: 第二类将被《平等权利修正案》伤害的女性是妻子们。

sentences.en: With a message that traditional women's roles are a privilege.
sentences.zh: 传达出的信息是，传统的女性角色是一种特权。

sentences.en: The laws of every one of our 50 states make it the legal obligation of the husband to support his wife.
sentences.zh: 我们50个州中每一个州的法律都规定，丈夫有法律义务供养他的妻子。

sentences.en: And she organized a very effective grassroots campaign where women showed up in droves to push this message on state legislators who had to vote on this.
sentences.zh: 她组织了一场非常有效的基层运动，女性成群结队地向必须对此投票的州议员施压。

sentences.en: And it works.
sentences.zh: 而且奏效了。

sentences.en: It lost in Missouri, Nevada, North Carolina, Virginia, and now Florida.
sentences.zh: 它在密苏里州、内华达州、北卡罗来纳州、弗吉尼亚州和现在的佛罗里达州都失败了。

sentences.en: No other states are willing to adopt it.
sentences.zh: 没有其他州愿意通过它。

sentences.en: And the reason that matters is because in the original piece of legislation that had passed Congress, there was a deadline for when the states had to ratify.
sentences.zh: 之所以重要，是因为在最初通过国会的立法中，有一个关于各州必须何时批准的截止日期。

sentences.en: And in fact, a few states even go back and try and rescind their ratifications.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一些州甚至回头试图撤销它们的批准。

sentences.en: The latest skirmish in the pitched battle over ratification of the Equal Rights Amendment is now history.
sentences.zh: 关于《平等权利修正案》批准的激烈战斗中的最新冲突现在已成为历史。

sentences.en: And one of the casualties may very well be final passage of the amendment itself.
sentences.zh: 而其中一个牺牲品很可能就是该修正案的最终通过。

sentences.en: So by 1982, which is the ultimate deadline that Congress came up with, they're short.
sentences.zh: 所以到1982年，也就是国会设定的最终截止日期，他们还差一些。

sentences.en: This amendment has not met the legal requirements to become the 28th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 这项修正案没有达到成为第28修正案的法律要求。

sentences.en: So basically, you're saying by the early 1980s, this seems to be quite dead.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，你是说到了20世纪80年代初，这似乎已经彻底没戏了。

sentences.en: You might think so, but the debate begins about whether or not the time limit is something that should be taken seriously or whether that deadline was always meaningless.
sentences.zh: 你可能会这么认为，但关于时间限制是否应该被认真对待，或者那个截止日期是否一直毫无意义，辩论开始了。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Let's explain that.
sentences.zh: 让我们解释一下。

sentences.en: So constitutional amendments, first of all, each one has taken its own circuitous path to passing.
sentences.zh: 首先，宪法修正案每一项都有其独特的曲折通过路径。

sentences.en: And they don't normally have ratification deadlines.
sentences.zh: 而且它们通常没有批准截止日期。

sentences.en: An example is the 27th Amendment.
sentences.zh: 一个例子是第27修正案。

sentences.en: It was ratified in 1992.
sentences.zh: 它是在1992年被批准的。

sentences.en: That's two centuries after Congress first passed it.
sentences.zh: 那距离国会首次通过它已经过去了两个世纪。

sentences.en: So supporters of the ERA argue that the Constitution itself never mentions deadlines for an amendment.
sentences.zh: 所以《平等权利修正案》的支持者认为，宪法本身从未提到修正案的截止日期。

sentences.en: So they just are meaningless and do not exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以它们只是毫无意义，并不存在。

sentences.en: And on top of that, there's a real debate about this business of states trying to rescind their ratification.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，关于各州试图撤销其批准的行为，存在着真正的争论。

sentences.en: States have tried that in the past on other amendments, on the 14th and 15th amendments.
sentences.zh: 各州在过去的其他修正案中也尝试过，比如第14和第15修正案。

sentences.en: And their original ratifications were still counted in the final count that had those become part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 而它们最初的批准在最终计票中仍然被计算在内，使它们成为了宪法的一部分。

sentences.en: So there is some real legitimate gray area here.
sentences.zh: 所以这里确实存在一些合法的灰色地带。

sentences.en: There is a lot of legal gray area here, yes.
sentences.zh: 是的，这里确实有很多法律灰色地带。

sentences.en: So this thing just kind of sits on the shelf for decades until Donald Trump is elected president.
sentences.zh: 所以这件事就在架子上搁置了几十年，直到唐纳德·特朗普当选总统。

sentences.en: And three more Democratic Party-controlled state legislators, Nevada, Illinois, and Virginia,
sentences.zh: 又有三个由民主党控制的州议会，内华达州、伊利诺伊州和弗吉尼亚州，

sentences.en: who are motivated by women who are outraged that Trump has won and what this will mean for women's rights, not to mention the Me Too movement, which was at its peak, adopt the ERA.
sentences.zh: 受到那些对特朗普获胜感到愤怒的女性的激励，以及考虑到这对女性权利意味着什么，更不用说当时处于巅峰的“我也是”运动，通过了《平等权利修正案》。

sentences.en: So it suddenly hits the magic number of 38, three-quarters of the states.
sentences.zh: 所以它突然达到了38个州的那个神奇数字，即四分之三的州。

sentences.en: It has still been passed by Congress.
sentences.zh: 它仍然是由国会通过的。

sentences.en: So on paper, according to supporters, it has cleared all the bars.
sentences.zh: 所以在纸面上，根据支持者的说法，它已经扫清了所有障碍。

sentences.en: The ERA has been ratified and should be part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 《平等权利修正案》已经获得批准，应该成为宪法的一部分。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: If you believe that that congressional deadline is not real.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为那个国会截止日期不是真的。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: So if you think it has met all the legal requirements and that the deadline is not in the Constitution, all that is left to do at this point is basically paperwork.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你认为它已经满足了所有法律要求，且截止日期不在宪法中，那么此时剩下的基本上就是文书工作了。

sentences.en: The National Archivist, who's responsible for the certification and publication of constitutional amendments, just needs to publish the ERA as the 28th Amendment,
sentences.zh: 负责宪法修正案认证和公布的国家档案管理员，只需要公布《平等权利修正案》作为第28修正案，

sentences.en: and then it is part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 然后它就成为了宪法的一部分。

sentences.en: A really interesting argument.
sentences.zh: 一个非常有趣的论点。

sentences.en: But, and this is a big but, the Trump White House at the time issues a legal opinion saying that the archivists cannot do that, and that's because of the deadline.
sentences.zh: 但是，这是一个很大的“但是”，当时的特朗普白宫发布了一份法律意见，称档案管理员不能这样做，原因就是那个截止日期。

sentences.en: They say that Congress set that 1982 deadline, and that because of that, this is all null and void.
sentences.zh: 他们说国会设定了1982年的截止日期，正因为如此，这一切都是无效的。

sentences.en: Anything that happened after that is dead.
sentences.zh: 在那之后发生的任何事情都已作废。

sentences.en: And in 2022, when Biden is president, the Biden White House defends that position.
sentences.zh: 而在2022年，当拜登担任总统时，拜登白宫为这一立场进行了辩护。

sentences.en: The Trump position, that the deadline matters, and that this is not suddenly a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 即特朗普的立场，认为截止日期很重要，这并不是突然就成了宪法修正案。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: So, again, we are in a legal gray area.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们又处于一个法律灰色地带。

sentences.en: In 2023, supporters of the ERA go to federal court to get a ruling about the deadline issue, and they lose.
sentences.zh: 2023年，《平等权利修正案》的支持者向联邦法院寻求关于截止日期问题的裁决，但他们败诉了。

sentences.en: A federal court says that the deadline is real.
sentences.zh: 联邦法院表示截止日期是真实的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, it's looking less gray, and the chances of the Equal Rights Amendment becoming part of the Constitution are looking less likely.
sentences.zh: 所以，情况看起来不那么模糊了，《平等权利修正案》成为宪法一部分的可能性看起来越来越小。

sentences.en: But, over the past few months, Democrats have decided to give it a final try.
sentences.zh: 但是，在过去几个月里，民主党人决定做最后一次尝试。

sentences.en: And what does that even mean, really?
sentences.zh: 那到底意味着什么呢？

sentences.en: After Roe was overturned, Democrats saw this as more urgent than ever, that the ERA could be a tool to protect abortion rights at the federal level,
sentences.zh: 在《罗诉韦德案》被推翻后，民主党人认为这比以往任何时候都更紧迫，认为《平等权利修正案》可以成为在联邦层面保护堕胎权的工具，

sentences.en: that it could anchor a right to an abortion in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 它可以将堕胎权锚定在宪法中。

sentences.en: And they have a Democratic president with the power to make this happen.
sentences.zh: 而且他们有一位有权实现这一目标的民主党总统。

sentences.en: They want to just treat this like it's already the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 他们想直接把它当作已经是国家法律来对待。

sentences.en: It's passed Congress.
sentences.zh: 它已经通过了国会。

sentences.en: It's got the three-quarters of states ratified.
sentences.zh: 它已经获得了四分之三州的批准。

sentences.en: Just order the archivist to publish it.
sentences.zh: 直接命令档案管理员公布它。

sentences.en: And, sure, it'll invite a legal challenge, but that's the next step.
sentences.zh: 当然，这会招致法律挑战，但那是下一步的事。

sentences.en: So, they literally say all Joe Biden has to do is pick up the phone, have a two-minute phone conversation with the archivist, order her to publish it,
sentences.zh: 所以，他们实际上说乔·拜登所要做的就是拿起电话，与档案管理员进行两分钟的通话，命令她公布它，

sentences.en: and then they'll deal with whatever comes next after that.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会处理随之而来的任何事情。

sentences.en: Forty-five senators, including Chuck Schumer, the majority leader, have written a letter to Biden saying, pick up the phone and call.
sentences.zh: 包括多数党领袖查克·舒默在内的45名参议员写信给拜登说，拿起电话打过去。

sentences.en: House Democrats, over 100, all saying, pick up the phone.
sentences.zh: 超过100名众议院民主党人，都在说，拿起电话。

sentences.en: Yes, it will invite a court challenge, but the point is that this would dare Republicans to have a legal battle to take away equal rights for women, to say, no,
sentences.zh: 是的，它会招致法院挑战，但重点是这将挑战共和党人，让他们进行一场法律战来剥夺女性的平等权利，让他们说，不，

sentences.en: we're fighting against this very simple amendment that says women deserve equal rights.
sentences.zh: 我们正在反对这个非常简单的修正案，它说女性理应享有平等权利。

sentences.en: Dare them to start that legal battle.
sentences.zh: 挑战他们去开启那场法律战。

sentences.en: And the lawmaker who has really taken up this mantle is the junior senator from New York, Kirsten Gillibrand,
sentences.zh: 而真正承担起这一重任的议员是来自纽约州的初级参议员克里斯汀·吉利布兰德。

sentences.en: who has made it a priority to persuade Biden that he can and he must do something on this,
sentences.zh: 是谁把说服拜登相信他能够且必须在此事上采取行动作为优先事项，

sentences.en: that he is the president who can make the Equal Rights Amendment part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 相信他就是那位能让《平等权利修正案》成为宪法一部分的总统。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Lowe.
sentences.zh: 我是维娜·洛。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《纽约时报》游戏中的《Connections》谜题，而且我热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，也喜欢尝试捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你们刚才听到的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Good morning, Senator Gillibrand.
sentences.zh: 早上好，吉利布兰德参议员。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: I'm well.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你呢？

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.en: It's nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: I reached Senator Kirsten Gillibrand inside her office on Capitol Hill last week.
sentences.zh: 上周，我在国会山的办公室里采访了克里斯汀·吉利布兰德参议员。

sentences.en: Sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: And thank you for putting on headphones.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你戴上耳机。

sentences.en: I know it is not the most glamorous way to start your day, but...
sentences.zh: 我知道这不是开始一天工作最光鲜亮丽的方式，但是……

sentences.en: I don't mind.
sentences.zh: 我不介意。

sentences.en: I wonder if you can, just to start, remember when you first learned that equal rights for women were not mentioned in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，首先，你是否还记得你最初是什么时候了解到宪法中并未提及女性平等权利的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 记得。

sentences.en: Well, I've known for a long time that the Equal Rights Amendment is not part of the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我很早就知道《平等权利修正案》不是宪法的一部分。

sentences.en: Recently, I started looking into the law and looking into actually what it takes to make a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 最近，我开始研究法律，研究通过一项宪法修正案到底需要什么。

sentences.en: And I realized pretty quickly it was about Article 5 of the Constitution that sets out two things that need to be accomplished to become a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 我很快意识到，这关乎宪法第五条，它规定了成为宪法修正案需要完成的两件事。

sentences.en: You need two-thirds of the House and Senate to vote in favor of it.
sentences.zh: 你需要参众两院三分之二的投票支持。

sentences.en: That happened in the 1970s.
sentences.zh: 这在20世纪70年代已经实现了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It needs three-quarters of the states to ratify.
sentences.zh: 它需要四分之三的州批准。

sentences.en: The last state to ratify was Virginia in 2020.
sentences.zh: 最后一个批准的州是2020年的弗吉尼亚州。

sentences.en: And so I realized really quickly that the two things that are required by the Constitution have been met.
sentences.zh: 所以我很快意识到，宪法要求的两件事都已经满足了。

sentences.en: So what's supposed to happen is when the two standards are met by Article 5, two-thirds House and Senate, pass it, ratified by three-quarters of the state,
sentences.zh: 所以应该发生的情况是，当第五条规定的两个标准——参众两院三分之二通过，以及四分之三的州批准——都达到时，

sentences.en: the archivist who has a ministerial job only, he or she is not supposed to analyze the law.
sentences.zh: 档案保管员，他只负责行政工作，他或她不应该去分析法律。

sentences.en: They're not supposed to have a deep think about it.
sentences.zh: 他们不应该对此进行深思。

sentences.en: They're just supposed to sign and publish when the two things are done.
sentences.zh: 他们只需要在两件事完成后签字并发布即可。

sentences.en: And because Trump was president in 2020, his Office of Legal Counsel issued a memo telling the archivist he couldn't sign and publish.
sentences.zh: 因为特朗普在2020年担任总统，他的法律顾问办公室发布了一份备忘录，告诉档案保管员不能签字发布。

sentences.en: And that memo said, timelines matter and you took too long to get this added to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 那份备忘录说，时间线很重要，你们花太长时间才把它加入宪法。

sentences.en: And they cited a decision saying that all constitutional amendments have to be done in a timely way.
sentences.zh: 他们引用了一项裁决，称所有宪法修正案都必须在合理的时间内完成。

sentences.en: Well, the 27th Amendment took 203 years to become a constitutional amendment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，第27条修正案花了203年才成为宪法修正案。

sentences.en: So clearly, timeliness is not a standard.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，及时性并不是一个标准。

sentences.en: And so I looked further into what the law says about timelines and whether this timeline that Congress had put in as a seven-years deadline in the preamble was actually constitutionally operative.
sentences.zh: 所以我进一步研究了法律关于时间线的规定，以及国会在序言中设定的七年期限是否真的具有宪法效力。

sentences.en: And there was actually precedent that talked about cases that had timelines and deadlines and saying they were not valid.
sentences.zh: 实际上有先例讨论过那些带有时间线和截止日期的案例，并称它们无效。

sentences.en: And I realized that the strength of the arguments were actually on our side.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，论点的力量实际上在我们这一边。

sentences.en: So I've been asking the White House to either issue a new OLC memo.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直要求白宫要么发布一份新的法律顾问办公室备忘录。

sentences.en: And if they don't want to do that, then direct the archivist to sign and publish on the basis that the two things that Article 5 requires have been completed.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不想这样做，那就指示档案保管员基于第五条要求的两件事已经完成的事实，进行签字和发布。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And we're going to get to all the ways in which you have brought and tried to bring that request to the Biden White House.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会谈到你向拜登白宫提出这一请求的所有方式。

sentences.en: But I think listeners will appreciate you explaining in a kind of bigger step back way why you and why so many other Democrats want the ERA now.
sentences.zh: 但我认为听众会感谢你以一种更宏观的角度解释，为什么你以及其他许多民主党人现在想要《平等权利修正案》。

sentences.en: Now, putting aside the legal arguments for just a moment, what in your mind does the Equal Rights Amendment achieve at this point that the country's current laws and jurisprudence,
sentences.zh: 现在，暂时撇开法律论点不谈，在你看来，《平等权利修正案》在这一点上能实现什么，而国家目前的法律和司法实践，

sentences.en: especially around the 14th Amendment's Equal Rights Clause, does not provide?
sentences.zh: 特别是围绕第14条修正案的平等权利条款，却无法提供的？

sentences.en: What gaps does it fill if it becomes the 28th Amendment of the Constitution?
sentences.zh: 如果它成为宪法第28条修正案，它能填补哪些空白？

sentences.en: Well, if you noticed in the Dobbs decision.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你注意到了多布斯案的裁决。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Overturning Roe.
sentences.zh: 推翻了罗诉韦德案。

sentences.en: Justice Alito alluded that there is no right to privacy in the Constitution and there's nothing protecting women for these issues in the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 阿利托大法官暗示宪法中没有隐私权，宪法中没有任何东西可以保护女性免受这些问题的影响。

sentences.en: Well, that really highlighted the need for the Equal Rights Amendment to be part of the Constitution because Equal Rights Amendments across the board in states,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这确实凸显了《平等权利修正案》成为宪法一部分的必要性，因为各州的《平等权利修正案》，

sentences.en: states like Connecticut, states like New Mexico, there's current litigations in places like Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 像康涅狄格州、新墨西哥州这样的州，在宾夕法尼亚州等地也有当前的诉讼。

sentences.en: When a state has an Equal Rights Amendment, in the case of reproductive rights, they have found that if a woman is denied access to health care for reproductive rights,
sentences.zh: 当一个州拥有《平等权利修正案》时，在生殖权利案件中，他们发现如果女性被拒绝获得生殖健康护理，

sentences.en: including abortion, that it's fundamentally unequal.
sentences.zh: 包括堕胎，那在根本上是不平等的。

sentences.en: And so in the cases of Connecticut and New Mexico, women on Medicaid were given access to abortion services because they were denied it.
sentences.zh: 因此在康涅狄格州和新墨西哥州的案件中，医疗补助计划下的女性获得了堕胎服务的机会，因为她们之前被拒绝了。

sentences.en: And they said that was unequal under the law.
sentences.zh: 他们说这在法律面前是不平等的。

sentences.en: So for you, the Equal Rights Amendment, perhaps not exclusively, but foremostly, is about creating in the Constitution a federal protection for abortion rights,
sentences.zh: 所以对你来说，《平等权利修正案》或许不是唯一，但首要的是在宪法中建立对堕胎权的联邦保护，

sentences.en: which you think has already happened in states whose constitutions have something similar to the Equal Rights Amendment in it.
sentences.zh: 你认为这在那些宪法中包含类似《平等权利修正案》内容的州已经实现了。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because if you have equality, let's just look at Dobbs.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你拥有平等，让我们看看多布斯案。

sentences.en: Dobbs ruled that women of reproductive years do not have a right to privacy.
sentences.zh: 多布斯案裁定育龄女性没有隐私权。

sentences.en: Red states have then implemented that to say women of reproductive years don't have the right to travel across state lines to get access to health care.
sentences.zh: 红州随后实施了这一裁决，称育龄女性没有跨州寻求医疗服务的权利。

sentences.en: They have decided women of reproductive years don't have a right to have private conversations on their Facebook pages with their mother about seeking abortion services.
sentences.zh: 他们决定育龄女性没有权利在Facebook页面上与母亲进行关于寻求堕胎服务的私人对话。

sentences.en: That women don't have the right to privacy to receive medicine in the mail.
sentences.zh: 女性没有隐私权通过邮寄接收药物。

sentences.en: Imagine how men in America would feel if they were told today that they, too, do not have the right to privacy, to cross state lines, or to receive medicine in the mail,
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果美国的男性今天被告知他们也没有隐私权，不能跨州旅行，不能通过邮寄接收药物，

sentences.en: or to have private conversations on social media with their families.
sentences.zh: 或者不能在社交媒体上与家人进行私人对话，他们会作何感想？

sentences.en: They would start a revolution.
sentences.zh: 他们会发动革命的。

sentences.en: And so I believe if we had an Equal Rights Amendment, Dobbs would be vitiated.
sentences.zh: 所以我相信如果我们有《平等权利修正案》，多布斯案就会失效。

sentences.en: Dobbs would no longer count because it is applying a standard to women only based on their gender that they don't have a right to privacy and therefore have no access to the health care that they need.
sentences.zh: 多布斯案将不再成立，因为它仅基于性别对女性适用了一个标准，即她们没有隐私权，因此无法获得她们需要的医疗服务。

sentences.en: That's a pretty big and important claim, and I wonder if it's at all disputed, you'd know better than I would,
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常重大且重要的主张，我想知道这是否受到任何质疑，你比我更清楚，

sentences.en: that explicitly prohibiting gender-based discrimination in the Constitution, which is what the Equal Rights Amendment would do, would, in your words, vitiate, obviate,
sentences.zh: 即在宪法中明确禁止基于性别的歧视——这正是《平等权利修正案》所做的——会用你的话来说，破坏、消除、

sentences.en: tear asunder the Dobbs decision entirely?
sentences.zh: 彻底撕碎多布斯案的裁决吗？

sentences.en: I think it could.
sentences.zh: 我认为可以。

sentences.en: It would be a strong legal argument that you are discriminating against women based on our gender and, in this instance, denying its access to life-saving care.
sentences.zh: 这将是一个强有力的法律论据，即你们基于我们的性别歧视女性，在这种情况下，拒绝了她们获得挽救生命护理的机会。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Once, Senator Gillibrand, you decide for all these reasons, both kind of legal and practical, that this is important to you, that you make this case to President Biden,
sentences.zh: 吉利布兰德参议员，一旦你因为所有这些法律和实践上的原因，决定这对你很重要，并向拜登总统提出这个理由，

sentences.en: what do you do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: What have you done so far to try to make this case to the President, to his aides?
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，你为了向总统和他的助手们提出这个理由做了什么？

sentences.en: I wonder if you can kind of walk us through all of that.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能带我们了解一下所有这些过程。

sentences.en: So, I started to ask for meetings with President Biden over a year ago.
sentences.zh: 所以，我从一年多前就开始要求与拜登总统会面。

sentences.en: I used every opportunity that I had with the President, or with the First Lady, or with Vice President Harris, or with Vice President Harris' husband,
sentences.zh: 我利用了一切机会，无论是与总统、第一夫人、哈里斯副总统、哈里斯副总统的丈夫，

sentences.en: or with their chiefs of staff, or with senior advisors in the administration, to make the case that the ERA is valid.
sentences.zh: 还是与他们的幕僚长，或政府中的高级顾问，来论证《平等权利修正案》是有效的。

sentences.en: And I have argued with his lawyer ad nauseum, and he disagrees with me, but I think my legal arguments are supported by far more people than support his.
sentences.zh: 我与他的律师争论了无数次，他不同意我的观点，但我认为支持我法律论点的人远多于支持他的人。

sentences.en: My argument's supported by the ABA.
sentences.zh: 我的论点得到了美国律师协会的支持。

sentences.en: The American Bar Association.
sentences.zh: 美国律师协会。

sentences.en: And my argument's supported by a number of attorneys general from dozens of states.
sentences.zh: 我的论点得到了数十个州的总检察长的支持。

sentences.en: And the weight of the law is on our side.
sentences.zh: 法律的力量在我们这一边。

sentences.en: Wait, should I intuit that you have not gotten this meeting?
sentences.zh: 等等，我是否可以理解为你还没有得到这次会面？

sentences.en: No, I have not gotten the meeting yet.
sentences.zh: 不，我还没有得到会面。

sentences.en: I'm still asking for the meeting.
sentences.zh: 我还在请求会面。

sentences.en: Mr. President, I would like to meet with you for five minutes.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，我想和您见五分钟。

sentences.en: I would like to make my best case to you.
sentences.zh: 我想向您陈述我最好的理由。

sentences.en: Forgive me for asking this.
sentences.zh: 请原谅我这样问。

sentences.en: Is it strange for you to have to essentially plead through intermediaries, whether perhaps in this moment we are one of them,
sentences.zh: 不得不通过中间人——也许此刻我们就是其中之一——来争取与总统进行一对一的交谈，这对你来说是否很奇怪？

sentences.en: to get a couple of moments one-on-one with the President?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道问题出在哪里。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know what the issue is.
sentences.zh: 我想也许是竞选活动阻碍了进程，因为它变成了一个问题：我们想在竞选期间做这件事吗？

sentences.en: I think perhaps the campaign got in the way, because it became a question as, do we want to do this in the middle of a campaign?
sentences.zh: 我们不应该等到竞选结束后吗？

sentences.en: Shouldn't we wait till after the campaign?
sentences.zh: 也许这些是顾虑。

sentences.en: Maybe those were concerns.
sentences.zh: 我们做了民意调查。

sentences.en: We did polling.
sentences.zh: 我们的民调显示美国人民支持这一点。

sentences.en: We have polling showing that the American people support this.
sentences.zh: 我们真的只是试图向所有高级顾问说明，这不仅在法律上是准确的，而且是正确的事情。

sentences.en: We've really just tried to make the case to all of the senior advisors that not only is this actually accurate legally, but that it is the right thing to do.
sentences.zh: 那么你是如何理解拜登总统似乎不愿参与此事的？

sentences.en: So how do you understand Senator Biden's seeming reluctance to engage this?
sentences.zh: 他没有和你见面。

sentences.en: He's not taking the meeting with you.
sentences.zh: 他没有公开谈论这件事。

sentences.en: He's not speaking out about this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道这是否是总统本人的意愿。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know that it's the president.
sentences.zh: 我认为是团队的问题。

sentences.en: I think it's the team.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我得告诉你，当我向他推销这个想法时，我是在拍照排队时利用那30秒的时间说的。

sentences.en: I got to tell you, when I pitched it to him, I pitched it to him with my 30 seconds that I had in a photo line.
sentences.zh: 在拍照排队时？

sentences.en: In a photo line?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 当拜登总统来到纽约庆祝石墙旅馆成为国家纪念碑时，我确保我排到了那个拍照队列。

sentences.en: When President Biden came to New York for the celebration of the Stonewall Inn as a national monument, I made sure I got to that photo line.
sentences.zh: 我说，总统先生，我认为您有机会指示档案保管员签字并发布《平等权利修正案》。

sentences.en: I said, Mr. President, I think you have an opportunity to direct the archivist to sign and publish the ERA.
sentences.zh: 你把它说出来了。

sentences.en: You got it out.
sentences.zh: 我说，如果您这样做，那将意义非凡。

sentences.en: I said, and if you do, it will be everything.
sentences.zh: 它将保障女性的生殖权利。

sentences.en: It will guarantee women reproductive rights.
sentences.zh: 它将保障她们在法律面前的平等。

sentences.en: It will guarantee them equality under the law.
sentences.zh: 它将成为您政府的基石。

sentences.en: It will be the cornerstone of your administration.
sentences.zh: 我说，您没有正式的角色，但档案保管员有，她需要勇气。

sentences.en: And I said, you don't have a formal role, but the archivist does, and she needs courage.
sentences.zh: 我相信如果您告诉她、指示她或发布一份新的法律顾问办公室备忘录，她会做的。

sentences.en: And I believe if you tell her or direct her or do a new OLC memo, she will do it.
sentences.zh: 他说，那么你是想让我大张旗鼓地宣传这件事吗？

sentences.en: And he said, so do you want me to make a big deal about it?
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，我想。

sentences.en: I said, yes, I do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的对话。

sentences.en: And that was our conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以是非常积极的。

sentences.en: So it was very positive.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有得到负面的反应。

sentences.en: So I've not had a negative reaction.
sentences.zh: 参议员，你认为也许阻碍他——如果不是他，也是他身边的人——的原因，

sentences.en: Do you think, Senator, that perhaps the thing that may be holding him, and if not him, those around him up here,
sentences.zh: 是他们担心这无法在基于1982年截止日期的不可避免的法律挑战中存活下来，他们只是认为这是徒劳且具有象征意义的吗？

sentences.en: is their fear that this won't survive the inevitable legal challenge that will come based on the 1982 deadline, that they just think that this is futile and symbolic?
sentences.zh: 听着，无论你采取什么方法来处理这个《平等权利修正案》，它最终都会上诉到最高法院。

sentences.en: Look, no matter what approach you take on this Equal Rights Amendment, it will go up to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是在不久的将来唯一可能的途径。

sentences.en: This is the only route that is possible, I think, in the near future.
sentences.zh: 为什么现在不把它作为一个机会，为你所信仰的事业挺身而出呢？

sentences.en: And why wouldn't you do it now as an opportunity to stand up for what you believe in?
sentences.zh: 你刚才提到了最高法院。

sentences.en: You just mentioned the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 你无疑知道最高法院伟大的自由派泰斗之一，鲁思·巴德·金斯伯格，在2020年曾说，她相信尽管世界，

sentences.en: You no doubt know that one of the great liberal lions of the Supreme Court, Ruth Bader Ginsburg, said in 2020 that she believed that as much as the world,
sentences.zh: 尽管国家需要《平等权利修正案》，但最好的做法，正确的方法，是重新开始。

sentences.en: as the country needed the ERA, that the best way to do it, the right way to do it, was to start over.
sentences.zh: 然而，她说——这是她的原话——我希望能看到一个新的开始，而不是试图仅仅采用当前的立法，

sentences.en: However, she said, and this is her quote, I would like to see a new beginning, rather than an effort to just take the current legislation,
sentences.zh: 在她看来已经错过了1982年的截止日期，现在就把它变成法律。

sentences.en: having missed the 1982 deadline in her mind, and make it law now.
sentences.zh: 那么，对于像她这样一位泰斗级的法律人物和理论上的盟友说“不，我认为你不能这样做”，你会怎么回应？

sentences.en: And so what do you say to a towering legal figure and theoretical ally like that saying, no, I don't think you can do this.
sentences.zh: “我认为你必须回到起点。”

sentences.en: I think you have to go back to the beginning.
sentences.zh: “你必须把这一切从头再做一遍。”

sentences.en: You have to do this whole thing all over again.
sentences.zh: 所以我不同意她的分析。

sentences.en: So I disagree with her analysis.
sentences.zh: 你必须明白，鲁思·巴德·金斯伯格是一位伟大的法律头脑。

sentences.en: And you have to understand, Ruth Bader Ginsburg was a great legal mind.
sentences.zh: 她是一位令人难以置信的学者和大法官，为我们的国家做了伟大的事情。

sentences.en: She was an unbelievable scholar and justice that did great things for our country.
sentences.zh: 但她对政治一窍不通。

sentences.en: She knows nothing about politics.
sentences.zh: 她对政治一窍不通。

sentences.en: It's not her job to understand politics.
sentences.zh: 理解政治并不是她的工作。

sentences.en: If you start over, you will never see reproductive freedom or equality for women in our lifetimes, because it's become a political wedge issue.
sentences.zh: 如果你从头再来，在我们有生之年将永远看不到女性的生育自由或平等，因为它已经变成了一个政治上的分歧议题。

sentences.en: So there are many people in the Senate today, in the House today, that if you ask them privately, do you believe women deserve equality?
sentences.zh: 所以今天在参议院和众议院里有许多人，如果你私下问他们，你认为女性应该享有平等吗？

sentences.en: They're going to say yes.
sentences.zh: 他们会说愿意。

sentences.en: But their vote on equality will be about their position on reproductive rights.
sentences.zh: 但他们关于平等的投票，将取决于他们在生育权利问题上的立场。

sentences.en: So that's the truth.
sentences.zh: 这就是真相。

sentences.en: And so I respect Justice Ginsburg for her legal acumen.
sentences.zh: 所以我尊重金斯伯格大法官的法律敏锐度。

sentences.en: I do not respect her view on this issue because I think she's wrong.
sentences.zh: 我不尊重她在这个问题上的观点，因为我认为她是错的。

sentences.en: Even, Senator, if you were to get President Biden to do this, a big if, you know that you face one last meaningful obstacle.
sentences.zh: 参议员，即使你能让拜登总统这样做——这还是个很大的假设——你也知道你面临着最后一个重大的障碍。

sentences.en: Because just a couple of days ago, the archivist came out, probably in response to your outspoken efforts here, and said, I will not do this.
sentences.zh: 因为就在几天前，档案保管员站了出来，很可能是为了回应你在这里直言不讳的努力，她说，我不会这么做。

sentences.en: I will not make the Equal Rights Amendment, the 28th Amendment to the Constitution.
sentences.zh: 我不会让《平等权利修正案》成为宪法第28条修正案。

sentences.en: Because in her legal analysis, her legal analysis, she's not a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 因为在她的法律分析中——她的法律分析，她又不是律师。

sentences.en: She knows nothing about the law.
sentences.zh: 她对法律一窍不通。

sentences.en: And for her to insert herself as a legal analyst in this whole process is unconstitutional.
sentences.zh: 她把自己当作法律分析师介入整个过程，这是违宪的。

sentences.en: She is supposed to publish the ERA because the two standards of Article 5 have been met.
sentences.zh: 她本应该公布《平等权利修正案》，因为第五条的两个标准都已经满足了。

sentences.en: I mean, your frustration is so palpable to me.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我能真切地感受到你的沮丧。

sentences.en: I've watched you.
sentences.zh: 我一直关注着你。

sentences.en: I've covered you for many years.
sentences.zh: 我报道你很多年了。

sentences.en: And I now have this vision of you, like, tiptoeing across the White House lawn at some ungodly hour and knocking on the front door.
sentences.zh: 我现在脑海里浮现出这样的画面：你在某个不合时宜的时间，蹑手蹑脚地穿过白宫草坪，然后敲响前门。

sentences.en: I mean.
sentences.zh: 我是说。

sentences.en: Well, I mentioned it in the Christmas party photo line.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在圣诞派对的合影排队时提过这件事。

sentences.en: And this is why I know Jill Biden knows about it.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我知道吉尔·拜登了解这件事。

sentences.en: I said, Mr. President, I'm still asking for five minutes to tell you about the Equal Rights Amendment.
sentences.zh: 我说，总统先生，我还是想请您给我五分钟时间，向您介绍一下《平等权利修正案》。

sentences.en: And Jill said, we know all about it.
sentences.zh: 吉尔说，我们对此非常了解。

sentences.en: I said, great.
sentences.zh: 我说，太好了。

sentences.en: I just need five minutes.
sentences.zh: 我只需要五分钟。

sentences.en: Because I really believe someone is advising him differently.
sentences.zh: 因为我真的相信有人在给他提供不同的建议。

sentences.en: And I don't think they know all the things I know.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为他们并不了解我所知道的一切。

sentences.en: And I would like to have him, at least as the President of the United States, make this decision fairly with all the information in front of him.
sentences.zh: 我希望他，至少作为美国总统，能在掌握所有信息的情况下公平地做出这个决定。

sentences.en: And let him, as the President, make history.
sentences.zh: 让他以总统的身份创造历史。

sentences.en: Lawyers write briefs.
sentences.zh: 律师撰写辩护状。

sentences.en: Presidents make history.
sentences.zh: 总统创造历史。

sentences.en: Well, Senator, thank you very much for your time.
sentences.zh: 好吧，参议员，非常感谢您抽出时间。

sentences.en: You're welcome.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Even as Republicans averted a government shutdown over the weekend, they exposed a deep rift between President-elect Trump and hardline House Republicans over spending and debt.
sentences.zh: 尽管共和党人在周末避免了政府停摆，但他们暴露了当选总统特朗普与强硬派众议院共和党人在支出和债务问题上的深刻分歧。

sentences.en: Trump had triggered the crisis by ordering House Republicans to raise the federal debt ceiling,
sentences.zh: 特朗普曾下令众议院共和党人提高联邦债务上限，从而引发了这场危机，

sentences.en: hoping that doing so before he was in office would avoid a messy showdown over the issue next year.
sentences.zh: 他希望在上任前完成此事，以避免明年在这一问题上出现混乱的摊牌。

sentences.en: Instead, nearly 40 House Republicans defied Trump, saying that his plan would generate too much debt.
sentences.zh: 然而，近40名众议院共和党人违抗了特朗普，称他的计划会产生过多的债务。

sentences.en: The spending package that ultimately avoided a shutdown, which passed both chambers of Congress on Saturday morning, extends current spending levels until mid-March,
sentences.zh: 最终避免停摆的支出方案于周六上午在国会两院通过，该方案将目前的支出水平延长至3月中旬，

sentences.en: and pushes the debate over the debt ceiling into next year, when Republicans will control the White House and both chambers of Congress.
sentences.zh: 并将关于债务上限的辩论推迟到明年，届时共和党人将控制白宫和国会两院。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Carlos Prieto, Luke Vanderploeg, Claire Tennesketter, and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由卡洛斯·普列托、卢克·范德普洛格、克莱尔·特内斯凯特和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans, with help from Paige Cowett, contains research help from Susan Lee, original music from Pat McCusker, Dan Powell, and Marian Lozano,
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威廉斯编辑，佩奇·考特协助，苏珊·李提供研究帮助，原创音乐由帕特·麦克卡斯克、丹·鲍威尔和玛丽安·洛萨诺创作，

sentences.en: and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 并由艾丽莎·莫克斯利进行工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Van Lansferk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和范·兰斯弗克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直陷入一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在《Metro》的最新一集中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《Metro》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你收听播客的地方订阅收听。
